items.text: Be subject to your parents in a free servitude.
items.quote: Thou dost subject child to parent in a sort of free servitude

items.text: Exercise your authority over your children as a jurisdiction of love.
items.quote: and settest parent over child in a jurisdiction of love

items.text: Let the bond of faith bind you to your brothers and sisters more strongly and closely than the bond of blood.
items.quote: Thou bindest brethren to brethren by the bond of religion, stronger and closer then the bond of blood

items.text: Bring children into the world and form them, for God instituted the family for the generation and formation of offspring.
items.quote: the family, instituted directly by God for its peculiar purpose, the generation and formation of offspring

items.text: Educate your offspring; this duty is given by God and cannot be surrendered.
items.quote: The family therefore holds directly from the Creator the mission and hence the right to educate the offspring, a right inalienable because inseparably joined to the strict obligation.

items.text: As father, be the principle of education and discipline for your children.
items.quote: The father is the principle of generation, of education and discipline and of everything that bears upon the perfecting of human life.

items.text: Give your children a Christian education; your right over them is a duty subject to natural and divine law, not an absolute or despotic power.
items.quote: their right to educate is not an absolute and despotic one, but dependent on the natural and divine law

items.text: Keep Sunday for religious duties and for family life at home, and do not let it be usurped by other demands.
items.quote: the time which should be devoted to religious duties and to family life at home.

items.text: Give them a Christian education, directing them to their last end, God, since the family is one of the necessary societies into which man is born for this work.
items.quote: Education is essentially a social and not a mere individual activity. Now there are three necessary societies... the family and civil society...

items.text: Direct and watch the education of the adolescent, removing occasions of evil and providing occasions for good in his recreations and social intercourse.
items.quote: direct and watch the education of the adolescent... removing occasions of evil and providing occasions for good in his recreations and social intercourse.

items.text: Exercise extended and careful vigilance over the dangers that threaten inexperienced youth, especially impious and immoral books, cinema, and radio.
items.quote: More than ever nowadays an extended and careful vigilance is necessary, inasmuch as the dangers of moral and religious shipwreck are greater for inexperienced youth.

items.text: Forewarn and forearm them as Christians against the seductions and errors of the world.
items.quote: they should be forewarned and forearmed as Christians against the seductions and the errors of the world

items.text: Cooperate with divine grace in Christian education to form Christ in them.
items.quote: cooperate with divine grace in forming the true and perfect Christian, that is, to form Christ Himself in those regenerated by Baptism

items.text: When you must discuss delicate matters of purity with your son, be on your guard and do not descend to details, lest you kindle the sin you wish to extinguish.
items.quote: it is of the highest importance that a good father, while discussing with his son a matter so delicate, should be well on his guard and not descend to details

items.text: Set a clear and constant good example to your children, remembering that a well-ordered Christian family is the first and most effective environment for education.
items.quote: more efficacious in proportion to the clear and constant good example set, first by the parents, and then by the other members of the household.

items.text: If you are one of the other members of the household, after the parents set a clear and constant good example to the children.
items.quote: first by the parents, and then by the other members of the household.

items.text: Prepare yourself carefully for the fundamental duty of educating your children; do not let temporal cares make you neglect this duty.
items.quote: for the fundamental duty and obligation of educating their children, many parents have little or no preparation, immersed as they are in temporal cares.

items.text: Do not send your children away from home even in their tenderest years, for the decline of family education begins when children are removed from the domestic environment.
items.quote: causes children to be more and more frequently sent away from home even in their tenderest years.

items.text: Keep your children from being torn away to godless schools and associations; do not permit them to be formed in irreligion and hatred.
items.quote: children are actually being torn from the bosom of the family, to be formed … in godless schools and associations, to irreligion and hatred

items.text: Keep your child under your care before he reaches the use of reason; do not allow him to be removed or disposed of against your will.
items.quote: before reaching the use of reason, is under the father's care. Hence it would be contrary to natural justice if the child were removed from the care of its parents

items.text: Educate your child not merely to live, but to the full perfection of man and the state of virtue.
items.quote: Nature intends not merely the generation of the offspring, but also its development and advance to the perfection of man considered as man

items.text: See to your child's religious and moral education, physical and civic training, and temporal well-being.
items.quote: Parents are under a grave obligation to see to the religious and moral education of their children, as well as to their physical and civic training

items.text: Make every effort to keep your child's education under your own control in keeping with Christian duty, and refuse schools where impiety may be imbibed.
items.quote: make absolutely sure that the education of their children remain under their own control in keeping with their Christian duty

items.text: Have your Catholic-born children baptized and brought up as Christians.
items.quote: reminding parents of their duty, to have all Catholic-born children baptized and brought up as Christians

items.text: Do not make your educational authority absolute or despotic; subordinate it to your child's last end and to natural and divine law.
items.quote: it is necessarily subordinated to the last end and to natural and divine law

items.text: Do not send them to neutral or mixed schools; provide them Catholic education in Catholic schools, even at your own expense.
items.quote: support Catholic schools for their children entirely at their own expense; to this they feel obliged in conscience

items.text: Never cease sacrificing and working for the support and defense of their Catholic schools and for just laws securing that education.
items.quote: for the support and defense of their schools and for the securing of laws that will do them justice

items.text: Give your children religious, moral and civil training, with practical and specific application, and let your own exemplary life support it.
items.quote: warn Christian parents of their grave obligations ... the religious, moral and civil training of their children

items.text: Do not provoke your children to anger; avoid impatience, excessive severity, and lax discipline.
items.quote: And you, fathers, provoke not your children to anger.

items.text: Use the God-given authority of a parent for their proper upbringing in the fear of God, not for your own advantage.
items.quote: make right use of the authority given them by God ... for the proper up-bringing of their children in a holy and filial fear of God

items.text: Do not relax parental discipline, but check the growth of evil passions in their hearts.
items.quote: all too common relaxation of parental discipline which fails to check the growth of evil passions in the hearts of the younger generation

items.text: Make use of the Church's educational environment—sacraments, schools, associations—to train them in Christian piety.
items.quote: This educational environment of the Church embraces the Sacraments ... schools, associations and institutions ... established for the training of youth in Christian piety

items.text: Since the family alone cannot train them in arts and sciences, provide schools that are complementary to family and Church, not opposed to them.
items.quote: the school is by its very nature an institution subsidiary and complementary to the family and to the Church

items.text: Do not send them to neutral or mixed non-Catholic schools; choose schools where all teaching is regulated by the Christian spirit under the Church.
items.quote: the frequenting of non-Catholic schools, whether neutral or mixed ... is forbidden for Catholic children
items.conflict: Parents must test all teaching by Scripture; no earthly church may forbid all non-Catholic education (1 Thess 5:21; Col 2:8).

items.text: Do not be satisfied with mere religious instruction; ensure that every subject is permeated with Christian piety.
items.quote: It is necessary not only that religious instruction be given to the young at certain fixed times, but also that every other subject taught, be permeated with Christian piety.

items.text: Give your child a religious, moral, physical, and civil education and provide for his temporal good.
items.quote: Parentes gravissima obligatione tenentur prolis educationem tum religiosam et moralem, tum physicam et civilem pro viribus curandi, et etiam temporali eorum bono providendi.

items.text: Raise him as a Christian and keep him out of schools where he may drink the poison of impiety.
items.quote: educere liberos, uti par est, more christiano, maximeque prohibere scholis iis, a quibus periculum est ne malum venenum imbibant impietatis.

items.text: Aim not only at begetting him, but at bringing him up to the full state of virtue.
items.quote: Non enim intendit natura solum generationem prolis, sed etiam traductionem et promotionem usque ad perfectum statum hominis in quantum homo est, qui est virtutis status.

items.text: Keep him in your care until he has the use of reason; it is against natural justice to take him away.
items.quote: de iure naturali est quod filius, antequam habeat usum rationis, sit sub cura patris.

items.text: Be the source of your child's upbringing, discipline, and all that perfects human life.
items.quote: Pater est principium et generationis et educatonis et disciplinae, et omnium quae ad perfectionem humanae vitae pertinent.

items.text: Do not provoke your children to anger.
items.quote: Patres, nolite ad iracundiam provocare filios vestros.

items.text: Drive out the folly bound up in your child's heart with the rod of discipline.
items.quote: Stultitia colligata est in corde pueri: et virga disciplinae fugabit eam.

items.text: Keep the authority over your child that belongs to parents; no state may extinguish or absorb it.
items.quote: Patria potestas est eiusmodi, ut nec extingui, neque absorberi a republica possit, quia idem et commune habet cum ipsa hominum vita principium.

items.text: Be subject to your parents in a willing service.
items.quote: Tu parentibus filios libera quadam servitute subiungis.

items.text: Govern your child with a devoted authority.
items.quote: parentes filiis pia dominatione praeponis.

items.text: Let the bond of faith unite you to your siblings more tightly than blood.
items.quote: Tu fratribus fratres religionis vinculo firmiore atque arctiore quam sanguinis nectis.

items.text: As the one who nurtures and directs your child, prepare him for his duties.
items.quote: those who nurture him and direct his destiny have the right coupled with the high duty, to recognize, and prepare him for additional duties.
